{"description":"Per-session selection of which design a session is attached to, replacing --graph-path fixed for the process lifetime.

SELECTION IS BY graph_id, NOT BY PATH. A path is a property of the server's filesystem and leaks it to clients; graph_id is the durable name the design already answers to, and the registry maps id to path. This also matches how identity already works — graph_id, the version stamp and the sync marker live in sidecar files designed to be read BEFORE the design is opened.

Preferred carrier is an HTTP path prefix (/g/<graph_id>/), because the selection is then visible in logs and routable by ordinary proxies. An MCP initialize parameter is the second option. A tool call that attaches the session is the worst: it makes every session stateful in a way a reconnect silently loses, and it leaves a window in which a session is connected to nothing.

Contributes an answer to dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design, which holds this as an open shape question.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"A session names the design it wants by graph_id, and the server maps id to path","provenance":"authored","status":"in_progress","tier":"operational"}
